at_a_glance.attests: The whole observation object: the transaction hash asked about, what the chain said, the block height, the chain head at reading, the confirmations, the moment observed, the desk's battery, and the binding — what, if anything, ties the transaction to one payment authorization (none, authorization_nonce or the reserved input_commitment), beside what was asked. When a facilitator's settlement response was supplied, input_claims is signed too: the sha256 of the bytes received and a per-field table of whether each claim agrees with the chain — never the claimed values themselves, echoed outside the signature under received_not_observed. The projection beside the artifact is signed on its own, points back by evidence_hash, and is never the record. Observations signed before 2026-09-11 carry neither battery nor binding: read that as predating binding classes, never as unbound; a battery cited without a binding is defective. From battery v3, a nonce checked against a successful receipt adds signed binding.evidence: pairing result, reason and, when readable, authorizer, nonce, recipient, atomic amount and receipt positions — one canonical USDC AuthorizationUsed immediately followed by its Transfer, every supplied term matching; ambiguous authorizers need payer, unknown ordering stays unestablished. Battery v2's independent nonce and transfer matches can overstate correspondence: consult /corrections before citing its binding claim. Battery v4 also checks the EVM receipt's transaction identity, reported chain, block height, chain head and status before signing; malformed provider answers, and missing or duplicate batch answers, are refused rather than labelled. From settlement-attestation-v5, a signed auth_capture field names each USDC leg that touched the x402 auth-capture escrow set (role, deployment, direction, source); absent, none did; status and binding never move for it. Historical signed bytes are unchanged; a sheaf (attestation_bundle) is this artifact at volume, every member signed alone.

Instant. Every artifact carries a cert_id and verifies free at https://scvd.store/api/verify/{cert_id}.

at_a_glance.does_not_attest: That goods or services were delivered, that a NOT_FOUND will never settle later, or that the payment was legitimate. That the transaction was the settlement of any particular request: binding says what it ties, and authorization_nonce ties one EIP-3009 authorization, not one 402 challenge — whether the door tied that nonce to a single request is the door's work and unobserved. Under auth-capture, the lifecycle: whether the hold auth_capture names was later captured, voided or refunded was not read. Anything a facilitator's settlement response says: it is received, not observed, and an agreement row that reads disagrees is a finding about the response, not a verdict on anyone. One RPC read of public state, at one moment, signed by a party with no interest in the answer.

One pass a day is conformance cadence, never uptime. Nor is it bought. The watched party pays — the rating agency's model, whose one defect is that the rater drifts favorable — so the terms say it at spec level: payment buys frequency and permanence, never outcome. An endpoint that degrades while its operator is paying gets signed readouts saying so, in public, at the URL the operator paid for. The clause rides every watch history as who_pays_and_what_it_buys.
